questions.q: In "A community is people, not a number Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: A mentor with community-management experience reviews your safety steps.
Define success: number of active members, replies per post, members who post themselves, number of reports handled.
Ask 10 members for a short feedback note: what is useful, what to change.
Describe a community you like online. Why do people stay?

questions.q: In "Kick-off circle Understand", which of these is a key idea?
o: The mentor agrees the evidence you will produce in this module: a 4-week content plan, a moderation log, an engagement table and a safety review.
Hold one live session or meet-up and note attendance.
Write three lessons learned and one decision: grow, hand over to member moderators, or close kindly.
A mentor with community-management experience reviews your safety steps.

questions.q: In "Set up and plan Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Helpful-reply share: 12 of 40 replies came from members, not the host (30%).
Posts 5 a week, replies 40 in week 4: 8 replies per post.
Write the community rules in 5 lines: kindness, no hate, no spam, privacy, how to report.
Plan 4 weeks of posts: a mix of useful tips, questions to the group, member stories (with permission), and a weekly meet-up or live talk.

questions.q: In "Moderation, safety and content policy Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Each week record: new members, active members, posts, replies, reports, actions taken.
Content policy: what is allowed, what is not, how to handle misinformation and arguments, how to credit others' work, copyright awareness.
Adjust the plan to what members valued most.
Give two peers written feedback: one thing that is strong, one thing to fix.

questions.q: In "Run the community for four weeks Apply", which of these is a key idea?
o: Handle at least one difficult moment using your policy and record what you did and why.
Invite the first 20 people personally: friends, colleagues, people who already care. Tell them why.
Moderation log: 9 reports, 8 handled within a day (89%), 1 in 2 days.
A mentor with community-management experience reviews your safety steps.
